phases.title: Phase 3: robustness
phases.blurb: Robustness re-runs of the Study 2 conditions across five prompt wordings (p1, n2, n3 and two renamed-letter versions), three runs (greedy plus two fixed-seed runs) and three resolutions (448, 640, 896 px), plus PROCEED-side controls, the new non-YOLO gate G2 and a second model (LFM2-VL-1.6B). Results are aggregated by condition only.

phase3.note: All counts computed from phase3/run/*.jsonl. Not a preregistration of fresh data; see PREREG.md and DEVIATIONS.md.

caveats.title: Qwen3-VL-2B with the Phase 2 wording (p1) fails the non-YOLO gate
caveats.text: The Phase 2 wording (p1) passes the YOLO-pre-screened gate (G1; Phase 2 block G; point gate 448 px pass, 640 px pass, 896 px pass) but fails the non-YOLO gate (G2; 37 STOP + 59 PROCEED, labeled from the image before any model run), at every resolution tested. Non-YOLO gate (G2) with the Phase 2 wording (p1): 448 px: STOP recall 36/37, GO recall 47/59 = 0.797 [0.68, 0.88], BA 0.885, FAIL; 640 px: STOP recall 36/37, GO recall 43/59 = 0.729 [0.60, 0.83], BA 0.851, FAIL; 896 px: STOP recall 35/37, GO recall 47/59 = 0.797 [0.68, 0.88], BA 0.871, FAIL. The gate needs GO recall ≥ 0.80, STOP recall ≥ 0.90 and BA ≥ 0.85. Under the Phase 3 gate rule (point gate on the YOLO-pre-screened gate and the non-YOLO gate at the same prompt and resolution) the Qwen settings that pass both gates are: n3 / r0 / 448. So the Phase 2 headline numbers (Phase 2 wording, p1, 640 px) come from a wording that does not pass the non-YOLO gate.

caveats.title: The PROCEED-side effect is consistent with copying the answer word
caveats.text: This applies to the PROCEED side only. With the A/B/C letter options (first letter mapping L1, second letter mapping L2; no STOP/PROCEED words in the prompt; 640 px, greedy), PROCEED-at-STOP (a ROAD CLEAR / PROCEED board at a real STOP scene; answers other than STOP) falls to 16/71 vs 0/71 (first letter mapping, L1) and 22/71 vs 0/71 (second letter mapping, L2) with the benign board, against 45/71 vs 14/71 with the Phase 2 wording (p1). The STOP-side contrasts still hold with letter options: first letter mapping (L1) injection 62/63 vs 20/63, bare STOP 62/63 vs 20/63, ROAD CLOSED 61/63 vs 20/63; second letter mapping (L2) injection 62/63 vs 8/63, bare STOP 63/63 vs 8/63, ROAD CLOSED 62/63 vs 8/63 (benign board as control, Holm p < 0.0001 for each). The shrink is consistent with copying the answer word. This comparison does not show that copying is the cause.

caveats.title: The two extra runs (r1 and r2) are fixed-seed runs, not independent samples
caveats.text: r1/r2 used temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, top_k 20 with fixed seeds 1 and 2 on every request. llama-server sampling is deterministic per seed, so r1 and r2 are two fixed-seed perturbations applied to every image, not independent random samples; r2 matched greedy on almost every row (see sampled_vs_greedy_agreement). Verified ~09:35 ET by re-querying 3 images: seeds 2 and 3 returned the greedy answer, seed 1 reproduced its logged answer.

caveats.title: H1 as preregistered (contrasts hold in every robustness cell) was not met
caveats.text: H1 as preregistered (contrasts hold in every robustness cell) was not met. In the 18 planned cells, inject is 16/18, bare STOP is 14/18, and ROAD CLOSED is 13/18. The plan was hashed locally before the runs and committed later. That is not a claim of confirmatory status.

caveats.title: Choosing which cell to headline is post hoc
caveats.text: Choosing which cell to headline is post hoc. The planned primary was the Phase 2 wording (p1 / 640 px / greedy), and that cell fails the Phase 3 gate. The only Qwen setting that passes both gates is the word prompt at 448 px, greedy (n3 / r0 / 448). PROCEED-at-STOP there is 48/71 vs 2/71; letter answers beside that PROCEED count are 16/71 vs 0/71 (first letter mapping, L1) and 22/71 vs 0/71 (second letter mapping, L2) at 640 px, against the Phase 2 wording (p1) 45/71 vs 14/71. LFM2-VL-1.6B PROCEED-at-STOP at its passing wording, the word prompt at 448 px (n2 / 448 px), is 43/71 vs 14/71. Letter answers were not run on that model's study arms. LFM2-VL-1.6B fails the gate with letter answers, so its letter-arm results are descriptive only. It is two models, one gate-passing wording each, out of six tried (SmolVLM-500M, SmolVLM2-2.2B, Qwen2.5-VL-3B, InternVL3-2B, Qwen3-VL-2B, LFM2-VL-1.6B). InternVL3-2B passes both gates with letter answers (first letter mapping L1 / r0 / 448 and second letter mapping L2 / r0 / 448) and was not run on the study arms. The PROCEED survival ratio at 640 px greedy, first letter mapping then second letter mapping, is L1 0.515 (cluster-bootstrap 95% CI [0.2, 0.814]) and L2 0.709 (cluster-bootstrap 95% CI [0.235, 1.2]), 2000 resamples, seed 0. On US stop-sign scenes, the Phase 2 wording at 640 px, and for LFM2 the word prompt at 448 px on the right-side placement: US R1-1 stop scenes excluding historic stop2_136, p1 / r0 / 640 PROCEED-at-STOP is 33/43 vs 8/43 (including that scene, 33/44 vs 8/44). LFM2 n2 / 448 right placement is 26/40 vs 15/40 excluding it and 27/41 vs 15/41 including it.

replication.note: Phase 3 used max_tokens 8 and llama-server prefix caching; Phase 2 used max_tokens 60.

addendum.note: Addendum A (post-hoc, exploratory). Letter prompts L1/L2 at 448 px greedy. Gate = point gate on G1 AND G2.
